title: Worked sizing example
symptom: None while the fleet is at or above its floor. Below the floor the per-worker rate limiters saturate and local activities queue.
cause: Concurrency limit fixes slots per worker, the rate limit fixes the fleet floor, latency fixes the timeouts.
fix: Size slots = connections / max workers, rate = limit / max workers, keep the fleet at or above the floor.
watch: API req/s and in-flight stay under their limits at 8 and 10 workers; at 6 workers the fleet's rate cap drops below demand and local activity latency climbs.

phases.name: 8 workers (sized floor)
phases.note: Guide inputs at this SCALE. Fleet at the computed minimum. Java: the per-worker rate limit is a token bucket inside the activity.

phases.name: 10 workers (autoscaler max)
phases.note: Per-worker caps were sized for 10, so the fleet cap equals the API limit exactly.

phases.name: 6 workers (below the floor)
phases.note: Fleet rate cap = 6 x per-worker rate < demand: calls wait for tokens (inside the activity, holding a slot).

title: API slowdown holds workflow tasks open
symptom: Workflow task latency and schedule-to-start rise together; queries (and signals/updates) lag.
cause: API slowdown keeps workflow tasks open; workflow task slots fill.
fix: Tight ScheduleToClose; circuit breaker in the activity; fail fast to a fallback.
watch: Workflow task execution latency, query latency, workflow task heartbeats and end-to-end latency in the broken window; breaker state and 'deferred' results in the fixed window.

phases.name: API 15x slower, patient policy
phases.note: StartToClose 10 s, ScheduleToClose 30 s, unlimited retries, no breaker, no fallback.

phases.name: API 15x slower, budgeted + breaker + fallback
phases.note: ScheduleToClose 2 s, StartToClose 500 ms, breaker opens at 50% failures, workflow returns 'deferred'.

title: Local activity slots exhausted
symptom: Local activities pile up waiting for a slot.
cause: Local activity slots sized from average latency, not Little's law at p99 and burst.
fix: Re-derive slots from Little's law; set ScheduleToStart so starvation fails visibly (Java supports it for local activities).
watch: Local activity slots available hits 0; end-to-end LA latency (schedule to completion) diverges from execution latency; with ScheduleToStart the overflow fails in 500 ms instead of waiting.

phases.name: 1 slot per worker, API 3.5x slower
phases.note: Little's law: ~8 calls/s/worker x ~165 ms = 1.3 concurrent > 1 slot. ScheduleToClose 30 s, no ScheduleToStart: the wait is hidden.

phases.name: sized slots + ScheduleToStart 500 ms, API 3.5x slower
phases.note: Slots = API concurrency / max workers; ScheduleToClose 2 s; ScheduleToStart 500 ms.

title: Slow call triggers workflow task heartbeats
symptom: History shows extra workflow task completions mid-call; queries wait ~8 s.
cause: A call passed 80% of the workflow task timeout (8 s of 10 s).
fix: Shorten the call or move it to a regular activity.
watch: Workflow task heartbeats per workflow and query latency for the risk-check flow; both drop when risk runs as a regular activity.

phases.name: 10 s risk check as a local activity
phases.note: Risk vendor p50 9 s. The SDK heartbeats the workflow task at 8 s (WORKFLOW_TASK_HEARTBEAT_COEFFICIENT = 4/5).

phases.name: risk check as a regular activity
phases.note: The workflow task completes right after scheduling the activity; queries are answered immediately.

title: Pod loss: ~10 s latency spike
symptom: Latency spike of ~10 s after a deploy or pod loss.
cause: Worker died mid-task; the workflow waits out the workflow task timeout before another worker retries it.
fix: Graceful shutdown that drains workflow tasks (WorkerFactory.shutdown() + awaitTermination); keep the default task timeout.
watch: Max end-to-end latency jumps to 10 s+ and workflow task timeouts appear after the crash; the graceful restart shows neither.

phases.name: kill -9 worker-a (half the fleet)
phases.note: Runtime.halt(): in-flight workflow tasks on worker-a are abandoned.

phases.name: graceful restart of worker-a
phases.note: SIGTERM path: WorkerFactory.shutdown() stops polling, awaitTermination(15 s) drains in-flight tasks, then exit.

title: Duplicate charges after a crash
cause: Workflow task retry re-ran completed local activities.
fix: Idempotency key per workflow ID and step; dedupe on the API side.
watch: Duplicate side effects at the API after the first crash (no key); idempotent replays instead after the second crash (key).

title: 429s after the fleet scales out
symptom: API returns 429 only at some times of day.
cause: Fleet scaled out past the size the per-worker cap assumed.
fix: Size caps for the maximum fleet, or use a shared limiter.
watch: API rejections (rate) appear only when 10 workers run caps sized for 6; caps sized for 10 or a shared limiter keep API req/s at the limit.

phases.name: 6 workers, caps sized for 6
phases.note: Per-worker rate = limit / 6. Fine while the fleet really is 6.

phases.name: peak: 10 workers, caps still sized for 6
phases.note: Fleet cap = 10 x limit/6 = 1.67x the API limit; demand 1.8x base exceeds the API limit.

phases.name: peak: 10 workers, caps sized for 10
phases.note: Fleet cap = API limit. Excess demand waits (and some fails fast) in the workers instead of hitting the API.

phases.name: peak: 10 workers, shared limiter
phases.note: No per-worker cap; every call takes a token from the fleet-wide limiter.

title: Outage turns into a retry storm
symptom: API outage multiplies its own load.
cause: Every workflow retrying in process at short backoffs.
fix: MaximumAttempts cap, circuit breaker, non-retryable errors for client faults.
watch: API requests/s (503) during each outage window: dozens of times the normal rate when broken, near zero once the breaker opens.

phases.name: outage: 250 ms constant retries, no cap
phases.note: Unlimited attempts every 250 ms for 10 s, invalid cards retried too, no per-worker rate cap.

phases.name: outage: capped retries + breaker + fallback
phases.note: 4 attempts with backoff inside 2 s, InvalidRequest non-retryable, breaker fails fast, result 'deferred'.

title: Retry-After above the local retry threshold
symptom: Many timers and workflow tasks per workflow.
cause: Backoffs or Retry-After above the local retry threshold (Java default: 3 x workflow task timeout = 30 s).
fix: Keep backoffs under the threshold; hand long waits to a regular activity.
watch: Timers and workflow tasks per workflow from sampled histories.

phases.name: 429 Retry-After 40 s honoured by the local activity
phases.note: 40 s > the 30 s threshold: the SDK records the attempt and starts a durable timer, then a new workflow task.

phases.name: long waits handed to a regular activity
phases.note: Retry-After > 1 s fails the local activity fast; the step is retried by a regular activity, server-side.

title: One crash re-runs a chain of calls
cause: Long chain of local activities in one workflow task, no checkpoint.
fix: Put a regular activity or a durable step between groups; keep chains short.
watch: API re-executions by step after each crash: all five steps re-run without checkpoints, only the last group with them.

phases.name: 5 local calls, no checkpoint; crash worker-a
checkpoint every 2 calls; crash worker-a
phases.note: A 1 ms timer after every 2 local calls completes the workflow task and persists their markers.

title: Resource-based tuner admits too many calls
symptom: Resource-based tuner admits far more concurrent calls than the API allows.
cause: I/O-bound calls don't move JVM CPU or heap, so the supplier keeps issuing slots.
fix: Fixed-size (or custom) slot supplier for local activities.
watch: Local activity slots used and API in-flight vs the concurrency limit; concurrency rejections only with the resource-based tuner.

phases.name: resource-based LA slots, API 8x slower
phases.note: Demand needs ~47 concurrent calls; the API allows 40 (at SCALE 0.2).

phases.name: fixed-size LA slots, API 8x slower
phases.note: Slots cap the fleet below the API limit; overflow fails fast to 'deferred' in the worker.
